prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: a production atlas of circular illustrated tokens for Creation, an original elemental myth about making a vast living world. The reference is the APPROVED STYLE AND CONTINUITY anchor, not a sheet to copy unchanged. Paint new subjects in exactly that family: luminous opaque gouache, selective fine ink contours, strong simplified silhouettes readable at 64px; deep lapis interiors, jade and turquoise, burnt ochre, muted coral, warm ivory light, very narrow ivory-gold rims. Not glossy coins or flat generic pictograms. Each icon is a complete perfect CIRCLE with opaque painted interior and transparent empty space outside. Center each circle in its own equal grid cell, circle diameter 80 percent of the shorter cell side, generous empty gutters. Absolutely no letters, names, numbers, grid lines, labels, UI, watermark or cast shadows outside circles. No modern laboratory hardware, books, houses or buildings. Only the specified object inside each circle, with a simple dark ground or essential local context. Tiny details must not carry the meaning. Related states should differ in structure, not merely colour. Follow item order exactly, left to right, top to bottom. Exactly 20 circles in 5 columns and 4 rows. Landscape atlas. Exact cell subjects: CELL 1, Light: A single brilliant ivory point releases a broad diagonal beam through ultramarine darkness; the beam visibly opens into empty space. Distinguish: Dominant ray and point, with no spherical stellar surface, flame tongues or field of separate stars. CELL 2, Dust: A loose diagonal spray of small dry ochre grains and uneven flakes, with individual particles separated by dark space. Distinguish: Sparse plain grains; enriched dust has varied reflective inclusions, sediment has settled layers, dense cloud has a coherent body. CELL 3, Mist: A low, translucent jade-white veil folds into two soft overlapping wisps, with dark background still visible through its body. Distinguish: Soft transparent veil rather than a solid cloud bank, dry grains or open ribbon-shaped wind. CELL 4, Gravity: Three unequal rocky spheres lie along narrowing curved paths toward one larger dark sphere; the nearest small sphere is visibly closest to the large mass. Keep the paths fine and the masses prominent. Distinguish: Convergence toward one mass; no symmetric magnetic loops, flat disk or tipped globe axis. CELL 5, Dense cloud: A compact indigo and jade cosmic cloud has a very dark dense knot at its centre and pale granular edges folded inward. No star shines inside it yet. Distinguish: One dark unlit knot, distinct from diffuse mist, a nursery with multiple bright embryos and an illuminated remnant. CELL 6, Starfield: A loose irregular scatter of separate ivory and warm-white stars occupies the circle, with clear dark gaps and no connecting lines. Distinguish: Dispersed independent lights rather than a spiral, a connected pattern or marks on stone. CELL 7, Massive star: An enormous blue-white stellar disk fills most of the circle, its intensely bright limb surrounded by a thick hot halo. Preserve the rounded surface and avoid tongues of fire. Distinguish: Much greater visual weight and hotter hue than the solitary first star; no exposed interior. CELL 8, Fusing core: A cutaway of a luminous star exposes a small white central core nested inside three broad coral and ochre shells, with tiny paired grains becoming denser clusters in the innermost shell. Distinguish: Stellar shell cutaway with luminous fusion centre, not a rocky planetary shell or released grains. CELL 9, Supernova: A fierce white central flash throws broad coral ejecta fingers outward in every direction, with torn stellar layers visibly separating from the centre. Distinguish: Active radial stellar explosion without a colliding globe, landscape or settled hollow shell. CELL 10, Heavy elements: Within a dark cutaway wedge of stellar material, several compact clusters of ivory, coral and metallic ochre grains sit tightly packed, enclosed by a curved glowing stellar shell. This is an atlas convention for heavier nuclei still inside a star. Distinguish: Dense grain clusters contained in stellar material; no molecular chains, dust spray or planetary metal sphere. CELL 11, Expanding remnant: A broad hollow shell of ragged coral gas surrounds a dark evacuated centre, with sparse fragments continuing outward beyond its rim. The initial blinding flash has passed. Distinguish: Empty centre and expanding shell rather than a bright explosion centre or soft illuminated cloud. CELL 12, Glowing nebula: Filmy jade and coral gas folds glow across a dark central opening, edged with delicate ivory light and a few embedded points. The cloud is thin and luminous rather than solid. Distinguish: Soft illuminated filaments, without the remnant's enclosing shell or nursery's dense bright knots. CELL 13, Enriched dust: A diagonal cloud of fine dark grains contains larger ochre, coral and pale metallic flecks, all dispersed freely against deep blue. Several flecks show distinct bright edges. Distinguish: A mixed diffuse spray of enriched material; plain Dust lacks the contrasting inclusions, Heavy elements remain enclosed in a star. CELL 14, New stellar nursery: Three compact white-gold star embryos glow inside separate dense folds of one large jade and ultramarine cloud, with fine ochre grains gathered around them. Distinguish: Multiple embedded bright knots connected by dense dusty folds; not an unlit cloud or exposed stars. CELL 15, Sun: A warm ochre sun with a pale circular face and a short clean corona floats in dark blue space; its disk is calm and complete. Distinguish: Warm gold disk of moderate size, without flame tongues or the massive star's nearly full-frame blue-white glare. CELL 16, Planetary disk: A small golden sun sits inside a broad flat tilted disk of dusty ochre rings, with a clear central opening and scattered clumps along the disk. Distinguish: One central star and a smooth accretion plane rather than spiral arms of stars or converging bodies. CELL 17, Planetesimals: Four irregular rocky bodies of different sizes tumble together in empty blue space; the largest has a rough cratered edge and none is spherical. Distinguish: A few substantial irregular stones with dark gaps; no dust haze, completed globe or active collision. CELL 18, Rocky world: A solid round young planet has a dark ochre surface with the same hook-shaped raised landmass and two small satellite ridges used throughout this world, against deep blue space. No familiar Earth continent is present. Distinguish: Whole round planet with recurring non-Earth landform; crust is a close cross-section, continent is a flat coastal view. CELL 19, Magma ocean: The same round planet glows coral across most of its surface; a few dark cooling rafts outline the hooked landmass as cracks of bright molten rock divide them. Distinguish: Planet-wide molten surface rather than a cool globe, crust slice or single volcanic mountain. CELL 20, Iron core: A rocky planet is cut open to show a dense ochre-metal inner sphere surrounded by a broad coral liquid-metal layer and a thinner dark rocky mantle. Distinguish: Dense planetary metal centre inside rocky shells; no stellar glow, nuclear grain clusters or exterior field loops. Keep the common circle size and painted finish. Anatomical lineages matter: insects have six legs, birds feathered wings, bats membranous finger-supported wings. A depicted early cell is a symbolic magnified view, not a modern laboratory slide. The world is not Earth's recognizable map. People, if listed, have varied warm earth-brown complexions, simplified features and no modern objects. Never add people, plants or animals to a subject that predates them. Do not draw the subject names.
